 Order

Accused No.4 in crime no.46/2023 registered by Thilaknagar Police Station, Bengaluru city for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 506 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code (for short hereinafter referred to as 'IPC') is before this Court under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail.
2. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner and the learned High Court Government Pleader appearing for the respondent-State.

3. The case of the prosecution is that on the basis of the complaint lodged by one Pruthvi Honnegowda, dated 02.03.2023, Station House officer of Thilaknagar Police Station has registered FIR in crime no.46/2023 against one Hariyanna and four others for the aforesaid offences.

In the complaint, it is averred that the complainant had paid a sum of Rs.1,25,00,000/- through demand drafts from Karnataka State Co-operative Apex Bank Ltd, Jayanagar Branch, Bangalore in favour of Shyamsundar Raju and others towards purchase of land bearing survey no.35 of Sathanur village,
Jala Hobli, NC: 2023:KHC:33724 Yelahanka taluk, Bengaluru district.

entities.text: Karnataka State Co-operative Apex Bank Ltd
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The accused persons allegedly collected the demand drafts from the complainant on 04.12.2021.
The complainant further alleges that earlier he had issued demand drafts to the accused persons to the tune of Rs.2,75,00,000/-.
Subsequently accused persons had requested him to take back the demand drafts and transfer portion of the amount covered under the demand drafts to their Bank account.
Accordingly, the complainant allegedly transferred Rs.1,50,00,000/- to the account of the accused persons after taking back the demand drafts.
Subsequently Shyamsundar Raju informed the complainant that he has not received the demand drafts or the amount which was transferred to the bank account of the accused persons.

It is in this background complainant had approached the Police and lodged a complaint on 02.03.2023, which had resulted in registering FIR in crime no.46/2023.
4.
Apprehending arrest, the petitioner had filed Criminal Miscellaneous No.3064/2023 which was dismissed by LXVI Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru city, vide order dated 11.04.2023.

entities.text: LXVI Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru city
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is under these circumstances, the petitioner is before this Court.
The learned counsel for the petitioner reiterates the grounds urged in the petition and prays for grant of bail to the petitioner.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader has seriously opposed the petition and prays for dismissal of the petition.

7. From the perusal of the complaint averments, it is seen that the complainant had allegedly paid amount to Shyamsundar Raju and other accused persons in the year 2021 and subsequently accused persons had handed over certain demand drafts to the complainant with a request to transfer a portion of the amount covered under demand drafts through NEFT/RTFS.
Accordingly, the complainant had taken back the demand drafts and transferred amount of Rs.1,50,00,000/- to the accused persons.
As per the complaint averments, the said transfer was made by the complainant to the bank account of Sardar Shariff, Heriyanna Shetty and Raghu.
There is no transfer of any amount to the account of the petitioner herein.

In respect of the incident that had taken place in the year NC:
2023:KHC:33724 2021, belatedly complaint is lodged in the month of March 2023.
8. Under these circumstances, I am of the considered view that the petitioner has made out a prima facie case for grant of anticipatory bail.

Hence, the following:
ORDER The Criminal Petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioner in the event of his arrest in Crime No.46/2023 registered by Thilaknagar Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC, subject to the following conditions:
1. The Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of the copy of this order and shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-(One lakh only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the investigating officer.
Petitioner shall regularly appear before the Trial Court without fail unless exempted by the Trial Court for valid reasons.
3. Petitioner shall not tamper with the prosecution witness and he shall co-operate with the police for investigation and appear before them whenever called upon.

4. The petitioner shall not involve in similar offences in future;
Sd/-
